info.title: Azure AI Foundry (BASIC profile)
info.description:
Companion to policies/wizard-foundry-policy-basic.xml. Import this into APIM to create every operation the BASIC profile needs in one step, instead of hand-creating each Frontend form.

ON IMPORT: set the API URL suffix to exactly 'openai'. Copilot CLI with COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=azure discards any path on the base URL and always calls <origin>/openai/..., so any other suffix is unreachable from the CLI.

AFTER IMPORT:
1. Apply wizard-foundry-policy-basic.xml at API scope (all operations inherit it).
2. Apply wizard-foundry-policy-basic-models.xml at OPERATION scope on listModels only. It must not inherit the API policy, which parses a request body that a GET does not have.
3. Point the API at a backend whose Runtime URL ENDS IN /openai, e.g. https://<account>.openai.azure.us/openai. Neither policy rewrites the path for inference, so the /openai has to come from the backend.

Request and response bodies are intentionally schema-free: APIM passes them through untouched and the policy does the only reshaping that happens.

post.description: Responses API. Copilot CLI 1.0.81 was observed using this surface for gpt-5.1 with COPILOT_PROVIDER_WIRE_API unset, so it is required in practice, not optional.
Versionless v1 chat surface. Used by VS Code and most OpenAI-compatible clients, and by Copilot CLI when COPILOT_PROVIDER_AZURE_API_VERSION is left at its default.
Deployment-scoped chat surface. The Azure OpenAI SDK builds this shape when a dated api-version is configured, so create it alongside the versionless one to cover either mode.

get.description: Model discovery. Copilot CLI and JetBrains AI Assistant probe this BEFORE sending any chat; without it they report "Model '<name>' not found on provider (HTTP 404)" even though the deployment is healthy. Needs the operation-scoped policy, not the API one.
